title: Polynomial dual detects maps between relatively perfect complexes
statement:
Let $R\to A$ be a flat finitely presented homomorphism of arbitrary commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Fix a surjection $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$, where $n\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Work in ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with derived tensor computed on K-flat resolutions and internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-object ringed site. Put $C=C_{P\to A}(P[0])[n]\in D(A)$, where $C_{P\to A}$ is derived coinduction with precomposition action $(a h)(a')=h(a'a)$ [def-trf-derived-coinduction]. Call $T\in D(A)$ $R$-perfect if it is pseudo-coherent over $A$ [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] and there exist integers $a_T\leq b_T$ with $H^i(T\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q)=0$ for every $R$-module $Q$ and $i\notin[a_T,b_T]$. For every $R$-perfect $Z\in D(A)$,
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,Z)=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad Z=0.$$
Consequently, for every morphism $f:X\to Y$ between $R$-perfect objects, if $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,f)$ is an isomorphism then $f$ is an isomorphism. No diagonal dualizing condition on $Z,X,Y$, no Noetherianity, and no nonzero-ring hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Agent relative-perfect detection corollary of Tag 0A7C, lemma-dualizing, on residue-field fibres, together with relative-perfect Hom base change and derived Nakayama. The arbitrary-base assertion is not the statement of 0A7C.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flat-fp-presentation-noetherian-model] to the specified $\pi:P\twoheadrightarrow A$. Obtain $R_0\subset R$, $P_0=R_0[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A_0$ with $R_0\to A_0$ flat finitely presented and all three rings Noetherian, and $A=A_0\otimes_{R_0}R$, $P=P_0\otimes_{R_0}R$, compatibly with the given presentation. Put $C_0=C_{P_0\to A_0}(P_0[0])[n]$ with the same precomposition action as in the statement.

source.place: Tag 02JO, lemma-flat-finite-presentation-limit-flat; chosen-presentation enhancement stated in the cited model lemma.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-arbitrary-polynomial-dual-properties] to $R_0\to A_0$ and this surjection: $A_0[0]$ is perfect over $P_0$. Apply [lem-trf-algebraic-shriek-relative-perfect] to the same Noetherian rings: it gives $C_0\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(A_0)$ and the scalar isomorphism $h_0:A_0[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_0}(C_0,C_0)$. Its finite-type hypothesis follows from the finite presentation already supplied. Neither assertion is applied to the possibly non-Noetherian final ring $A$.

source.place: Tag 0BZW, lemma-relative-dualizing-algebraic (1)(a),(c),(2); polynomial perfectness as in the cited arbitrary-base node.

proof.text: For any prime $\mathfrak q\subset A_0$, the map $A_0\to(A_0)_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], and its target is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Hence [lem-trf-flat-coherent-homothety-base-change], applied to $C_0,C_0$, carries $h_0$ to an isomorphism $(A_0)_{\mathfrak q}[0]\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_{(A_0)_{\mathfrak q}}((C_0)_{\mathfrak q},(C_0)_{\mathfrak q})$. If $(C_0)_{\mathfrak q}=0$, this would make the nonzero local ring $(A_0)_{\mathfrak q}$ zero, a contradiction. Thus $C_0$ has full support, and [lem-sfb-noetherian-full-support-localizing-generation] gives $A_0[0]\in\operatorname{Loc}_{A_0}(C_0)$. When $A_0=0$ there are no primes and the same conclusion holds.

source.place: Tag 0A6A, lemma-base-change-RHom, flat bounded-target case; full-support localizing-generation corollary stated in the cited node.

proof.text: Check Tor independence for the polynomial square before applying coinduction base change. Choose a bounded finite-projective $P_0$-complex $F$ representing $A_0[0]$, available from step 2. The monomial description [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] makes $P_0$ free over $R_0$; the split-free description [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] then makes every $F^j$ flat over $R_0$. Both $F$ and $A_0[0]$ are K-flat over $R_0$ by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat], using flatness of $A_0/R_0$. Therefore the exact derived extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] is computed on these two representatives by $F\otimes_{R_0}R$ and $A_0\otimes_{R_0}R=A[0]$, which consequently represent the same object. On the other hand $F$ is K-flat over $P_0$, again by the bounded-flat lemma, and [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model] computes $A_0\otimes_{P_0}^{\mathbf L}P$ by $F\otimes_{P_0}P=F\otimes_{R_0}R$. This proves $A_0\otimes_{P_0}^{\mathbf L}P\simeq A[0]$, the needed Tor independence.

source.place: Tags 0661 (lemma-base-change-comparison) and 064K (lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism, bounded-above flat K-flat model); explicit resolution check for this square.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-perfect-coinduction-tor-independent-base-change] to $P_0\to A_0$ and $P_0\to P$. Its hypotheses are precisely perfectness in step 2 and Tor independence in step 4. At $N=P_0[0]$, and then shifting by $n$, it gives an isomorphism $C_0\otimes_{A_0}^{\mathbf L}A\cong C_{P\to A}(P[0])[n]=C$ in $D(A)$. In particular this preserves the coinduced $A$-action; an isomorphism merely after forgetting to $P$ would not suffice.

source.place: Tags 0A6A and 0661; coinduced-action enhancement as stated in the cited base-change lemma.

proof.text: Let $L=-\otimes_{A_0}^{\mathbf L}A:D(A_0)\to D(A)$. It is exact by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and is the left adjoint to restriction in [def-zl-ring-derived-scalar-extension]. Thus it preserves coproducts: for every family $V_i$ and every $W$, adjunction identifies maps $L(\bigoplus_iV_i)\to W$ with $\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(LV_i,W)$, which is the coproduct universal property. The preimage under $L$ of $\operatorname{Loc}_A(C)$ is consequently closed under all the operations defining $\operatorname{Loc}$ (functors also preserve retractions). By step 5 it contains $C_0$, so it contains $A_0[0]$ by step 3. Since $L(A_0[0])=A[0]$, we obtain $A[0]\in\operatorname{Loc}_A(C)$.

source.place: Tag 0GMT, lemma-tensor-hom-adjoint, and Tag 06Y6, lemma-derived-base-change; elementary preimage-of-localizing-hull argument.

proof.text: Now let $Z$ be any object of $D(A)$ with $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,Z)=0$. Closed tensor--Hom adjunction [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(C,Z[j])$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(A[0],R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,Z)[j])$, hence these groups vanish for all $j$. Let $\mathcal S$ be the full class of $V$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(V,Z[j])=0$ for every $j$. Exactness of Hom out of distinguished triangles [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact] makes $\mathcal S$ closed under triangles and shifts. The coproduct universal property makes it closed under coproducts, and a retract of zero Hom groups is zero, so it is closed under retracts. Thus $\mathcal S$ contains $\operatorname{Loc}_A(C)$, in particular $A[0]$. By [lem-pc-derived-module-free-generation], every object of $D(A)$ belongs to the localizing hull of $A[0]$, so $Z\in\mathcal S$. Taking $j=0$ gives $1_Z=0$, which makes $Z$ a zero object. This proves the requested implication, in fact without using relative perfection of $Z$.

For a morphism $f:X\to Y$ as in the statement, choose its cone triangle $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\to T\to X[1]$. The functor $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,-)$ takes this to a distinguished triangle by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. If its first map is an isomorphism, [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] gives $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,T)=0$. The stronger detection for all $T\in D(A)$ established in step 7 gives $T=0$, and the same zero-cone criterion applied to the original triangle proves that $f$ is an isomorphism. This also covers zero objects and the zero ring.

source.place: Exactness of derived Hom and the zero-cone criterion for distinguished triangles.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0BZW over a flat Noetherian model (Tag 02JO), full-support generation by residue-field extraction and Noetherian induction, then perfect coinduction base change and extension of the localizing hull. This avoids an unjustified tensoring of the bounded-below Hom complex of Tag 0E1U.

This is the first delivery and live still has the item unsplit with no repair note, so it is not superseded. Steps: (1) the model node keeps the given surjection pi, which steps 4 and 5 need to identify P0 tensor R with P and A0 tensor_{P0} P with A. (2) polynomial-dual-properties gives A0 perfect over P0; algebraic-shriek-relative-perfect is applied only to the Noetherian rings R0 and A0 and gives C0 bounded with finitely generated cohomology and h0 an isomorphism. (3) Localization is flat with Noetherian target, and the homothety base-change node gives h an isomorphism at every prime q, so (C0)_q is nonzero and C0 has full support; A0=0 also holds. (4) Tor independence: F has R0-flat terms, F and A0 are K-flat over R0, lem-pur computes the scalar extension on each, and the source-K-flat tensor model gives A0 tensor^L_{P0} P = A; no flatness of R0 to R is used, and n=0 is fine. (5) The perfect coinduction base-change node with N=P0[0] gives C0 tensor^L A isomorphic to C in D(A). (6) Pulling back the localizing hull Loc(C) along the coproduct-preserving exact functor puts A in Loc(C). (7) By the closed adjunction and free generation, every Z with RHom(C,Z)=0 is zero; this is stronger than the target and does not weaken it. (8) Cone triangle and zero-cone criterion. New nodes: the flat Noetherian model is true by 02JO(3) on R_i[x]/(f) with 00FN; it is not a duplicate of pbc-flat-finite-presentation-model, trf-flat-subring-model-system or a1-fppf-integer-model, none of which keeps the given presentation. Full-support localizing generation is Neeman's support theorem; I checked the report's proof (residue-field retract, Noetherian induction via 00L0/00L4, telescope), and the cases B=0, a non-perfect E and an E without full support behave as stated.
